note: DESIGN NOTES — the two readings this node had to settle (Q1/Q2), and the two measurements behind them. (1) Q2 ANSWERED BY REVERSAL, NAMED: the .ann/archive/** snapshot commits in the SAME commit as the archive's live-tree deletions. 12/20 read the snapshot as the operator's deliverable and left it out of scope; measured live, that reading is what makes the engine's own archive dirty, because a renameSync is ONE change spanning two trees — half-staging it is not a smaller commit, it is a dirty tree that refuses the NEXT archive. engineWriteDirs() therefore names .ann/archive, and the reversal is pinned by test with the reason, not just the behaviour. (2) Q1 UNCHANGED: the delivery commit stays the operator's act — a source edit beside a tooling write commits the tooling path only and leaves the source dirty (re-asserted under the widened journal). (3) MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED — how git stages a removal: `git add -- <pathspec>` stages a removal for a pathspec naming a gone FILE even inside a mixed pathspec list, but a pathspec naming a gone (or present-but-empty) DIRECTORY stages NOTHING once mixed with other pathspecs (add, add -A and add -u all fail mixed; each works alone). A deletion record is therefore EXPANDED through `git ls-files -z -- <rel>` — the INDEX, never a worktree scan — with a fallback to the path itself. (4) MEASURED — a rename is invisible to `git show --name-only`: it collapses to the destination, so the e2e asserts on `--name-status` and takes BOTH halves. (5) EVERY PATH IS RESOLVED ON BOTH SIDES OF EVERY COMPARISON: the rules/ symlink points onto .ann/rules and git refuses a pathspec beyond a symbolic link, and the macOS temp dir is itself a symlink (/var to /private/var), so resolving one side only would make a real path look out of scope. (6) THE EXCLUSION SET IS A READABLE CONSTANT (neverStaged): the write-rev ledger and its .tmp, logs/** (the provider op-log records prompts), and the provider config (mode 0600, may hold the API key). A reviewer reads one list instead of reconstructing a predicate. (7) A REFUSED WRITE JOURNALS NOTHING — pinned per writer (an in-force spec name, a taken brief name, a bad staged-doc name): the journal is a fact about what was WRITTEN, so a refusal cannot claim a write it did not make. (8) FIXTURE CHANGE, HONESTLY NAMED: `docs --write` now moves HEAD, so the close-gesture e2e had to commit the deliverable BEFORE reading the sha it cites — the capture's own sha is the bytes the run saw (= HEAD at capture time), and a sha read any earlier would no longer bind (no-captured-pass). That is the fixture catching up to the new behaviour, not a weakened assertion.
